course_description:
Analyses economics of modern banking theory and financial institutions management. Describes various types of financial institutions and examines means of managing their operations.

The course introduces students to the Australian financial system, and provides an overview of a financial system in a developed economy by describing its main components. Theﾠcourseﾠexplains the role of a financial system in the economy, the functioning of financial markets, the main characteristics of common financial products, the valuation of financial assets, the nature and management of financial institutions, the role of central banks in the payment system and the regulation of the financial system. Thus, the course does not exclusively focus on financial institutions management issues, as the title may suggest, but aimsﾠat providing aﾠwide picture of the different components making the Australian financial system, components that are present in a form or another in the financial systems of all developed economies.

The course provides the background recommended for students who plan to take more advanced topics in Financial Economics such as ECON3210 Financial Markets and Institutions. Although not a formal requirement, the course is also useful for students planning to study FINM2401 Financial Management, FINM3401 Corporate Finance or FINM3404 Banking and Lending Decisions.ﾠ The course has also been designed to appeal to students outside the BEL Faculty who are interested in obtaining an overview of the operation of the financial system. A basic level of maths is required for the course.

course_aims:
The course aimsﾠto introduce the student to the role of the financial system in the economy, the functioning of the financial markets and its products, the nature and management of financial institutions, and the regulation of the financial system.

The course teaches the key concepts of the discipline providing an overview of the financial system, whichﾠis the context of many other Economics courses, asﾠwell as providing solid foundations for those contemplating further studies in the area of Financial Economics or Finance.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate comprehension of basic economics and finance news.
Demonstrate expertise in analysing and evaluating financial markets, instruments, and institutions.
Evaluate the validity of economic theory by contrasting it with real world data.
Analyse the implementation and impact of monetary policy in a modern economy.
Create an analysis of a course related topic and present it clearly and freely to a peer audience.

assessment_details.category: Practical/ Demonstration, Presentation, Project, Role play/ Simulation
assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Peer assessed, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Student create teams early in the semester and get allocated a topic that they have to analyse using the tools from class. The task is to use the knowledge from the workshop / textbook material combined with very limited independent research to present their topic to their fellow students. A detailed task sheet / marking rubric will be provided 2 weeks before presentations start. The presentation time slot will be allocated in coordination with the teams' preference and is OUTSIDE of workshop times. This presentation also serves as practice run for the more important end of semester presentation. Duration: 6 minutes for a team of 3 students + 5 minutes question time (smaller / larger teams require written exception and time is adjusted proportionately, i.e. 2 minutes per student) Format: Students present in allocated time slots. Simply reading (e.g, notes) is not allowed. All team members shall participate equally. All presentations are recorded. Read full task description Hide full task description
assessment_details.assessment_security: Secure assessment: This assessment is designed to protect academic integrity and assess your understanding of course concepts. You must only use the approved materials and tools for this assessment task. Use of prohibited materials in this task may be investigated and treated as academic misconduct. See assessment instructions for more details.
assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Presentation will be given at allocated / chosen timeslot. The performance during that presentation and Q&A is marked. The slide set submission after the presentation is just a formality required to receive the marks from the actual presentation.
This is a live presentation in front of a live audience.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 7 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
As this is a live team presentation delivered to an audience, extensions can be granted only in exceptional circumstances and supported by the evidences as per UQ-rules ( https://my.uq.edu.au/files/11502/evidence-assessment-extension-application.pdf ). Teams requesting an extension must also submit their current slide deck . As the presentation is developed over several weeks, an extension will normally be approved only where the submitted draft demonstrates appropriate progress at the time of application. Where a situation covers at least 8 days before the due date, the affected student will be separated from the team and offered an alternative individual oral assessment.
Late submission
You will receive a mark of 0 if this assessment is submitted late .
